key_insight: An annular spiral flow construction yields forced three-dimensional Navier–Stokes solutions whose energy dissipation stays uniformly positive along a sequence of viscosities tending to zero.
engineering_relevance: The construction provides a theoretical benchmark for studying how mixing can sustain energy dissipation at very low viscosity.
method: Wind a radial segment into a two-turn spiral, then apply alternating planar shears.
Track vertical velocity against sine profiles whose angular period halves after each shear pair, then let diffusion act.
Embed the planar construction in a (2+½)-dimensional framework to obtain smooth three-dimensional solutions with identical initial data.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a mathematical positive lower bound on dissipation over a fixed subannulus and one vertical period, with forces converging uniformly in time in C^α for every 0<α<1.
watch_item: This is a specially constructed forced-flow result along a viscosity sequence, not a demonstration for generic turbulent flows or engineering geometries.
paper_title: An Annular Spiral Construction for Anomalous Dissipation in the Forced Navier-Stokes Equations
